entries.stdout: JSON with one part for each check that ran: semantics (policy and diagnostics), code
entries.result: check, check all, check semantics and check code (ADR 0057): the semantics part is the shared whole-vault check result, and the code part is the code check answer (boards, findings, skipped, behind)
entries.diagnostics: actionable file locations and messages on stderr; the code check also writes each finding with its subject and evidence, one line per skip reason with a count (checkouts named), and behind per board and part
entries.semantics: checks YAML configuration and every semantic board family; invalid configuration activates defaults and warnings; unreadable families are errors; check code and check all run the code check (ADR 0046) on its own route, never the polled check: it reads every board at its current variant, or at the draft --variant names where a board has one, never a historical or shelved variant, and only files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, each language and format an adapter knows through code facts and every other file as text; it warns ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH and on a named draft BINDING_PATH_MISSING; from the evidence between each board's bound parts it reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part that code reaches with no relationship (a warning when resolved, information on candidates) and, for a relationship with no anchor, RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED as information, judged against the evidence kinds the vault configuration lets each relationship kind accept; across a network hop it joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code and sets the value to another part's address, as configured-path evidence (a compose service runs the directory it builds, and any of them the code drawn inside the part bound to it; a candidate where more than one runner sets the value differently or the address leads to more than one part), and an unsupported relationship whose kind accepts a configured path names the side with no evidence in missing, code or infrastructure (TASK-367.23); for each container bound to a module it holds the derived interface (ADR 0044) against what the module exposes (TypeScript: what its root files export; Python: what a package's __init__.py exposes; Swift: the open, public and package declarations of a target's files; C and C++: what a directory's public headers declare; Terraform and OpenTofu: a module directory's variables and outputs, which a call of it uses), warning ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED on an entry point that owns nothing exposed while a drawn caller's code reaches it from outside the module and CALLER_UNDRAWN on a hidden part whose exposed code an unbound outside file uses at run time, and telling EXPOSED_UNUSED as information for exposed names no file outside the module uses, a module it cannot read skipped as exposure-unknown, and for a Terraform module VARIABLE_PASSED_THROUGH (variables passed unchanged to one argument of a resource) and MODULE_SHALLOW (one resource, every variable passed through) as information; a part bound to a Terraform or OpenTofu root module (a directory of .tf or .tofu files) names an address of that root, read across the local modules it calls and never from state, variable files or .terraform, with no terraform or tofu run, and a reference that joins two such parts is resolved configured-path evidence (TASK-367.17); an address inside a remote module is skipped as module-not-read unless --plan, which may repeat, names a plan JSON from terraform show -json or tofu show -json inside a registered checkout for the root module of its directory, of which only addresses and references are read; it lists what it skipped with the reason, and its behind reading is information (ADR 0045); --variant, --every-draft and --plan belong to check, check all and check code, and check semantics refuses them as usage errors (ADR 0057)
entries.ordering: validate --variant against --every-draft; check semantics reads current policy and inspects every board; check code runs the code check, which refuses a named plan it does not read before the pass; check and check all run the semantics check, then the code check; report all diagnostics; exit 1 if a semantics diagnostic or a code check warning remains

entries.result: the board aggregate under its new name, or with the variant renamed

entries.semantics: renames the board, or with --variant one variant, and nothing else: ids, lifecycles, ancestry and adoption, shelving and reconciliation records stay; the old name is kept in formerNames and still opens the board or variant, the board file moves with its name, panes on it are pointed at the new name and the canvas's claim follows it; a name another board carries or carried, a variant name another variant answers to, a name that cannot address a board and the name it already has are refused
entries.ordering: former-name resolution, lease, expected-version check, transition, validation, new name's lease without waiting, file move, then one atomic write

entries.result: the board as it now stands in the target vault, both ends of the move (vault and repository identity, and what the command registered for the target), and every drill-down it rewrote

entries.semantics: moves the whole note, every variant, former name and id unchanged, into the vault found from --to as -C finds one, registering what holds it when the registry does not know it; drill-downs in the source vault into the board are rewritten to name the target's identity and the board's own into the source vault to name the source's; panes on the board follow it into the target vault, a target checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository becomes the chosen one, and the mover's claim ends; two checkouts of one identity, a name or former name the target has, a drill-down into an untracked vault and a holder of the board or of its name in the target are refused
entries.ordering: version stated, target vault found and registered, then on the server: the name's lease in the target and the board's lease in the source, expected-version check, refusals, the target note, each rewritten source board under its own lease without waiting, and the source note deleted last; a stopped move leaves the board in both vaults and the same move run again finishes it

entries.semantics: reads the aggregate as it is on disk; a document that is not coherent is refused

entries.result: one variant against the variant it is read against (the current variant, or on a board with none its direct predecessor; --against names another): first the interface changes of each container (entry points added and removed, parts moved between the interface and the hidden parts, callers gained and lost), then the five interface measures of each container on the variant, the one it is read against and each variant --beside names (repeatable), side by side, then every part, relationship, sequence, step, walkthrough and beat either of them has, its standing, and the fields that moved
entries.diagnostics: the comparison named, then one line per container whose interface moved, then one line per container with its measures on each variant read, then counts and one line per relationship that moved on stderr; usage/refusal on stderr
entries.semantics: derived from the whole variant before any view narrows it, by the same pure comparison the canvas and the renderer overlay run; relationships and steps carry the endpoints they now have, named as well as identified; an interface change is derived on both variants by the shared interface derivation and sets no standing on any part; the interface measures come from the same derivation per variant, mark no change and are never combined or ranked; an unknown --beside variant is a usage error; with no --against, the current variant and a first draft on a board with no current variant are refused
entries.ordering: read the board, resolve the variant, resolve the variant it is read against, resolve each --beside variant, compare and measure, then print

entries.result: one group of one variant (members, internal edges, directed boundary edges, immediate neighbors) or one container of one variant (entry points, hidden parts, callers, outgoing relationships, relationships onto the container itself, pass-through entry points, with the five counts), or the fact that the node holds no parts
entries.diagnostics: summary and vocabulary warnings on stderr; usage/refusal on stderr
entries.semantics: derived from the whole variant before any view narrows it, by the shared pure inspections and never stored; a configured empty group answers empty, an id neither configured nor used is refused; a container is read by id or by a name that fits one node, and a node with no children answers that it holds no parts; exactly one of --group and --container is given
entries.ordering: read the board, resolve the variant, read the policy for a group, inspect, then print

entries.result: the hotspots and change coupling of one variant of one board: the period read in each repository (the checkout's HEAD and its start and end), every part the lens read ranked by the commits of the period that changed its bound files, each part's commits newest first with subject, time and file count, the coupled pairs (two parts that changed together in at least 5 of those commits at a degree of at least 30%) with their shared commits, degree and whether nothing on the board joins them, how many large commits the count left out, and the parts the lens did not read with the reason
entries.diagnostics: the board and variant, the period of each repository, the parts that changed in it most commits first, how many parts had none, the coupled pairs highest degree first with the unjoined ones marked, how many large commits were left out and how many parts were skipped per reason on stderr; usage/refusal on stderr
entries.semantics: derived on request from Git through the files each part binds and never stored (ADR 0045, ADR 0015); reads the current variant or the draft --variant names, and refuses a historical or shelved variant; the period is the commits on the HEAD of each registered checkout from --since, or the year before the commit time of HEAD, up to HEAD, so one HEAD gives one answer; commits of more than 30 files are left out of every count and counted; parts with no binding, a drill-down, an unregistered repository or a ref the checkout does not have out are listed as skipped; change coupling pairs two parts bound into one repository that share at least 5 counted commits at a degree (shared commits over the mean of the two parts' counts, cut to whole percent) of at least 30%, thresholds fixed, leaves out a pair whose bound paths overlap, and marks a pair unjoined when no relationship or flow step joins the two parts, their containers or parts inside them and neither holds the other; the server keeps each answer in memory keyed on the board version, the options and each checkout's HEAD
entries.ordering: validate --since, ask the server, which reads the board, resolves the variant, snapshots the checkouts, walks each repository once, ranks the parts and pairs them, then print

entries.result: the parts of the board's current variant whose bound files the commits from the merge base of --base and HEAD up to HEAD (or up to --head, a ref read from Git without a checkout) changed, with each part's commits, the commits (large ones marked), each repository's merge base and head or why it was not read, and the parts skipped with the reason; with --variant the changed parts are split into named and changed, changed but not named, and named but not changed, and each named part says why
entries.diagnostics: a summary line, one line for each repository not read, and one line for each part of each list on stderr; usage/refusal on stderr
entries.semantics: information only: derived on request from Git and the board, never stored, no severity and no change to the exit status; --base is any ref that resolves in a registered checkout and nothing is fetched, so a checkout where it does not resolve is named and not read; HEAD of each checkout, or --head resolved as the code check resolves a ref, is read, with no uncommitted change; a checkout where --head does not resolve is named and not read, and one that no checkout resolves is refused with HEAD_UNRESOLVED; a proposal names a part that the comparison marks added, changed or removed and a part at either end of a relationship or step it marks; a part with no binding, a drill-down, an unregistered repository, a pinned ref the checkout does not have out, or an unread range is skipped and in none of the lists; --variant names a draft, and the current variant, a shelved or a historical variant is refused; the proposal is read against --against, else the current variant, else its parent, and a proposal with no parent on a board with no current variant names every part it holds; --against names a current variant or a draft other than the proposal
entries.ordering: read the board, resolve the current variant and the proposal, resolve the ref and its merge base in each checkout, walk the commits, map them onto the bound paths, then print

workflows.name: device-trust stencil to bound node
workflows.evidence: These operations can express separate human intent, and the current evidence is one device-trust workflow rather than a repeated released workflow.
workflows.decision: Do not create a task. Reconsider only after TASK-119 through TASK-122 provide production-backed completion or evaluation evidence of repeated caller-side identity reconstruction.

workflows.name: promote or demote a selection
workflows.evidence: Live selection is browser state. A caller may read stable ids from one explicit pane and deliberately pass them to a board write.
workflows.decision: retain the explicit two-step boundary; board writes never read selection

workflows.name: duplicate then operate on copies
workflows.evidence: Duplicate already returns copied elements and ids; callers should not need a recovery query.
workflows.decision: reject collapse; enforce complete duplicate result

workflows.name: query then arrange
workflows.evidence: Choosing elements and choosing a layout operation are separate user intents and approval boundaries.

workflows.name: claim, several writes, release
workflows.evidence: The explicit lease is what removes write gaps while each requested act remains one write.

workflows.name: versioned write chain
workflows.evidence: fingerprint.version is the optimistic-concurrency handle for the next independent act.

workflows.name: render and export
workflows.evidence: Camera movement, browser pixels, and document export have different owners and side effects.

workflows.name: replace import
workflows.evidence: One requested replacement currently clears and batches as two board writes.
workflows.decision: Track independently; do not implement in TASK-123.01.

workflows.name: snapshot restore
workflows.evidence: One requested restore currently clears and batches as two board writes.
workflows.decision: Track independently; do not implement in TASK-123.01.

workflows.name: TASK-119 through TASK-121 proposed commands
workflows.evidence: Those tasks must declare new contracts after this proof and must not be implemented here.
